turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sit. Palpitations, yes?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, but it's really nothing, doctor. Um, heart racing on and off for three weeks, roughly, mostly at night.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only at night?
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No, doctor. I'm his partner. Before office meetings also the heart starts going. He just won't say it straight.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Meetings, maybe. Exams got over last month. I'm not stressed, people make too much of it.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a little, if I climb to the fourth floor. Otherwise I'm completely fine. I play cricket on Sundays.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain with it?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blackout?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never happened.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Giddiness?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No giddiness.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever or sweating?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Sweating, no, only if the room is hot, which it isn't.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): How much coffee in a day?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Four cups, office filter coffee. And energy drinks, maybe two, sometimes not really that many.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He is minimising again. Afternoon he has a full can, Sting or Red Bull, and one more at night on the laptop.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vape or smoke?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Vape only. Hardly, a few puffs. Not cigarettes.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Every evening after dinner, that mango ice one, he doesn't stop till it's finished.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't drink. Waste of money, and my mother would finish me.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any medicines daily?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No tablets. I don't even take paracetamol unless I really have to, and I haven't.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thyroid or heart trouble in the family?
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His mother has thyroid. She takes a tablet every morning, since many years. Heart side, no attacks, not that I have heard.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Work or studying?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Both, kind of. I'm in articleship, CA, client meetings every week. Sleep is fine though.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is ninety... no, one hundred and eight. Blood pressure one-thirty over eighty-two. Saturation ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Ankles not swollen.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Then it's nothing, na? My friend had gastric and they did all this drama also.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not calling it nothing. Could be the caffeine, could be thyroid, could be a rhythm problem. Not sure yet.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): ECG today. Thyroid blood test, TSH and free T4.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Today itself? I have a meeting at four.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, today. Stop the energy drinks. Bring coffee down to one cup. Stop the vape.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): When the racing starts, breathe in for four counts and out for six. Do it.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): If the reports are normal, can he go back to one Red Bull? He will ask me tonight.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. Come back in two weeks with the reports. If he blacks out or the chest pain becomes real, come earlier.
